text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Washington says it backs Turkey's full membership of the European Union.
- Head of the armed forces tells president of his concern over growing radicalism of the ruling Islamists.
- Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller promises no more journalists will be imprisoned for what they write and says those already in jail will be released.
- Testimony of a far-rightist reveals that the military set a group of nationalist hitmen after the 1980 coup to carry out attacks for the state.
- Thirty-nine Kurdish rebels were killed by government troops in clashes in the southeast.
- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan vows to build mosque in Ankara's wealthy Cankaya residential area.
- Twenty-five state-owned enterprises in the Turkish Cypriot state will be privatised.
- Leftist opposition leader Bulent Ecevit calls for the government to be toppled within the parliamentary system and criticises calls for military intervention.
